subject: Pricing & SLA structure for Dedicated pool — A100/H100/L40S tradeoffs
messages:

Subject: Dedicated pool options — quick context and ask

Hi Neha,

Thanks again for taking the intro. We want to move from the pilot to a reserved Dedicated pool for inference in Q3. High level: 24/7 production traffic for our customer-facing chat assistant (avg 12k reqs/day, 95th token length ~450). Primary goals: predictable cost, stable p95 latency below 300ms, and an SLA for throughput so we can commit to enterprise customers.

We looked at model family options and have three shortlisted: smaller-custom on A100-80GB, H100-80GB for long-context, and L40S for cost-sensitive batches. Can you send a crisp breakdown of:
- perf/$ across these GPUs for our workload (cost per 1M tokens or per-1000-reqs),
- recommended pool sizing to guarantee p95 latency at 200 rps sustained with 2x buffer,
- reserved commit tiers and discount bands (12/24/36 mo),
- any SLAs or uptime/latency guarantees you can offer for Dedicated.

If helpful I attached our throughput sample file.

Cheers,
Anjali
EdgeAI — Head of Platform

Hi Anjali — thanks for the context and the sample. High-level answers up front, then I can send a short offer with numbers: 

1) Perf/$ (rough guidance for your profile):
   - H100-80GB: best p95 perf for long-context models and highest throughput per GPU; perf/$ wins if you need low p95 and large context; approx 1.0x baseline.
   - A100-80GB: ~0.75–0.85x H100 on the same model family; better if memory-fit is the constraint and you want slightly lower unit cost after discounts.
   - L40S (48GB): ~0.5–0.65x H100 depending on quantization and batch sizes; lowest list $/hour but less headroom for long KV caches.

2) Pool sizing: to hit 200 rps sustained at p95<300ms we usually recommend sizing for 2x expected burst headroom. Roughly: H100 x3–4 GPUs (depending on batching); A100 x4–6; L40S x6–9 for equivalent p95. We'll model with your actual token distributions for final numbers.

3) Reserved commits / discounts: standard bands are 10–15% for 12mo, 18–28% for 24mo, and 25–35% for 36mo depending on committed vGPU-hours and up-front payment. We can layer additional volume tier discounts when you commit multiple pools/regions.

4) SLAs: Dedicated includes a platform SLA for 99.95% control-plane availability; for data-plane throughput SLAs we offer custom SLOs tied to commit level (example: 99.5% throughput availability at committed rps for 24mo+). We include automated fallback to compatible model variants if capacity constraints occur.

I'll draft a two-option offer (conservative A100-pack and H100-performance pack) and include a mixed pool option with L40S for warm-cache cheaper capacity. Marcus and Karthik, can you run a quick cost model and a 24-mo pricing bucket for EdgeAI?

—Neha
Neha Kapoor

Neha / team — first-pass numbers attached (RI-Dedicated-Offer-v1.pdf + RI-Dedicated-Offer-v2.xlsx). Key assumptions called out on tab "Assumptions": your 200 rps target -> translates to ~600k tokens/hr at our median tokenization. Batching assumptions: we modeled mixed batching (5–12 token batches typical).

Headline options (monthly average cost, excl. tax):
- H100 pack (3x H100-80GB, 24-mo commit): $55k/mo after 22% discount. Expected p95 ~220ms with warm-cache.
- A100 pack (5x A100-80GB, 24-mo commit): $46k/mo after 20% discount. Expected p95 ~310ms under same load.
- Mixed (2x H100 + 3x L40S, 24-mo commit): $38k/mo after 24% blended discount — cheaper but more operational tuning required.

Notes on perf/$: H100 gives the best service-level consistency; A100 can be cheaper per-hour but may need additional instances for the same p95. L40S is attractive for stateless short-context inference and batch/embedding workloads.

Attachments: RI-Dedicated-Offer-v1.pdf (summary) and RI-Dedicated-Offer-v2.xlsx (cost model tabs + elastic scaling options).

Subject: Re: Dedicated pool options — counter and SLA language

Hi Anjali — good questions. Short answers and a concrete counter below.

SLA credits: yes — we can include a throughput credit ladder in the contract:
  - Missed throughput 99.0–99.5%: 10% credit of monthly committed fee
  - Missed throughput 98.0–99.0%: 25% credit
  - <98.0%: 50% credit + escalation
We tie credits to measured throughput on the committed rps for the pool, measured by our telemetry.

Accelerated discounts: we can improve the 36-mo band by another 6–8 points on top of the baseline if EdgeAI commits to a $750k ARR threshold or agrees to a year-2 pool refresh (we typically treat that as an exchange for newer GPUs at lower hour rates). Example: H100 36-mo could reach ~30–38% off list depending on payment terms.

L40S operational risks: main risks are KV cache pressure and longer tail latencies on long-context workloads. That shows up as higher p95 (often 1.5–2x worse) when a model's working set exceeds GPU memory and we must rely on host-side transfers. We mitigate with:
  - cache-aware routing (keep hot sessions on H100),
  - prefix caching to reduce re-computation,
  - mixed fleet with L40S for stateless bursts and H100 for hot, long sessions.

Concrete counter (24-mo / 36-mo options):
Option A — Performance Pack (H100):
  - 3x H100-80GB Dedicated GPUs, reserved 24-mo: $55k/mo (22% discount).
  - 36-mo with $750k ARR commit or year-2 refresh: $42k/mo effective (~35% discount).
  - Throughput SLA: 99.5% with the credit ladder above.

Option B — Hybrid Pack (H100 + L40S):
  - 2x H100 + 3x L40S, reserved 24-mo: $38k/mo (24% blended).
  - 36-mo escalate to $30k/mo effective with ARR or refresh commitment.
  - SLA: 99.0% throughput baseline; 99.5% available for Performance Pack only.

If these look reasonable I'd propose a short signature-ready term sheet (two pages) and then a 60–90 day proof-of-performance (pilot) to validate p95 numbers before the committed billing starts. Marcus — please attach a redlineable term-sheet and update the spreadsheet with the 36-mo band tweaks.

Thanks — happy to take this live tomorrow if Anjali prefers.

—Neha
